summary:
Project ŞEBİA (MOONBASE: MISSION SURVIVAL) is an interactive, web-based educational game and presentation platform designed to address the challenges of lunar exploration. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, our solution translates complex Artemis mission parameters—such as solar energy storage, water ice harvesting, regolith oxygen extraction, and radiation protection—into an engaging cooperative strategy experience.

In the game, 1 to 4 players take on specialized Artemis roles (Commander, Engineer, Geologist, Medic) to manage vital base resources and survive a 5-day lunar mission. Project ŞEBİA bridges the gap between raw NASA science and public accessibility by maintaining strict separation between real space data and fictional game mechanics. It is important because it fosters systems thinking, resource planning, and deep curiosity about space science, making it an ideal educational tool for classrooms and future space enthusiasts
details:
What It Does & How It Works MOONBASE: MISSION SURVIVAL (Project ŞEBİA) is an all-in-one interactive presentation and cooperative strategy game built directly into a single, zero-dependency web application. Designed for 1 to 4 players, the game places the crew at a lunar South Pole habitat where they must survive for 5 days. Each player takes on a specialized Artemis role—Commander, Engineer, Geologist, or Medic—and draws scenario cards involving critical mission trade-offs. Players must carefully balance four interconnected resources (Oxygen, Water, Energy, and Radiation Shield) alongside Crew Health, survive nightly resource drains and random space emergencies (such as solar flares or micro-meteoroid punctures), and spend Tech Points on base upgrades. At the end of the mission, players receive a comprehensive Mission Report analyzing their decisions, score breakdown, and survival metrics.

Tools, Coding Languages & Architecture We built the entire project using pure HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript. By packaging both the 6-slide scientific briefing and the playable game engine into a single lightweight file without external libraries, frameworks, or installation requirements, the project runs smoothly on any desktop or mobile browser—making it instantly accessible for classrooms and public outreach. We utilized CodePen as our primary platform for prototyping, testing, and public demonstration.

Creativity, Benefits & Key Considerations Our main design priority was scientific honesty. Instead of mixing real aerospace data with arbitrary game mechanics, every single card and interface element clearly separates verified NASA research (marked in green with direct source links to NASA HRP, LRO, LCROSS, and Artemis documentation) from fictional game points (marked in amber). By turning complex lunar engineering constraints—such as the 15-Earth-day lunar night, abrasive regolith dust, and In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU)—into tangible cause-and-effect gameplay, our project fosters systems thinking, teamwork, and genuine curiosity about NASA's Artemis missions.
